gaps.title: The camera never frames the person speaking
gaps.detail: Measured in the real game (index.html), 15 conversations in the meadow: state().field.camera.current stayed at 4.0 deg in 13 of 15 while the hero's facing swung from 23 to 326 deg, and camera.talkFraming reads 0 throughout. Nothing moves the lens when a conversation opens, so who is on screen is an accident of where the camera happened to be. Measured consequences in shots/P12-critic-c1/meadow: talkTo('nib') -> the ONLY face in frame is the hero's own, Nib Tolley is entirely off screen while his nameplate is up (11-m-nib.png); talkTo('thurl') and talkTo('wat') -> a different villager's bald head covers 15-25 percent of the frame and the speaker's nameplate sits over that stranger's chest (13-m-thurl.png, 14-m-wat.png); talkTo('budge') -> Fennick Quiddle's backpack covers the hero (09-m-budge.png); talkTo('tansy') -> Tansy is half off the bottom-right corner behind the text box (05-m-tansy.png); talkTo('cactuddle') in Puddlewick leaves it at the right edge behind the well. BUILD: when Dialogue opens with an npc, ease the field camera over 0.4-0.6s into a two-shot - orbit to (heroFacing +/- 20-25 deg), dist about 3.0-3.5, lookAt the midpoint of hero and speaker lifted to chest height, fov unchanged - hold it for the conversation, and release back to the walk orbit when it closes. Also add NPC bodies to the see-through candidate set: cameraOccluders(true) at orbit 250 with Mr Budge's head over 20 percent of the frame reports fading=[stone, wood] and tested=[], and the nearest list contains butterflies and robins but not one person, so a villager between the lens and the hero can never fade.

events.note: npc.js now solves a real two-shot when a conversation opens, instead of nudging. Geometry: with the lens at direction camDir from the hero, somebody at direction to lands at screen-x proportional to sin(to-camDir) and depth proportional to cos(to-camDir); phi = +/-180 is hidden behind the hero, phi = 0 is their back filling the frame. frameTalk() sends the orbit to phi = +/-128 deg (the nearer side, so the lens never takes the long way round), holds it for the whole speech (re-asserted every 0.5s, so the follow camera cannot ease back mid-line), pushes in to max(5.0, dist*0.94) and restores both on close. clearTheShot() also steps any villager standing on the lens-to-speaker line 1.05 units aside. New probe __DQ.talkShot() reports it. Measured in the real game: 21 of 21 conversations (9 in the meadow, 12 in Puddlewick) returned onScreen true, speaker at 24-75 percent across the frame and 16-49 percent down it; camera.talkFraming reads 0.997 while the box is up; talkTo nib, which the critic found with the boy's own face as the only one in frame, now gives ndc -0.24/0.247, xPct 38, head 44 percent down - Nib whole in shot. Shots: shots/P12-round3/after-two-shot-candlewick.png, after-four-people-one-scene.png.

Mostly solved but NOT closed, and the fix introduced a worse failure. Good news first, measured over 30 conversations in the real game (13 meadow + 17 Puddlewick): talkShot().onScreen is true 30/30, the speaker lands 31-67 percent across the frame and 9.7-51.6 percent down it, camera.talkFraming reads 1 while the box is up, and npcFacing = heroFacing +/- 180.0 in all 17 Puddlewick cases, so people do turn and face you. The failure: the new solve swings the lens without testing what it will be standing inside, and at the pond it buries the camera in geometry for the whole conversation. Deterministic repro, index.html, timeOfDay 10, talkTo in this order - pell, hen1, tansy, sausage, gudgeon: the Gudgeon frame is a flat dark-olive void. Measured over the 60 percent of the frame above the text box: mean luminance 43.9, fraction of pixels below luminance 55 = 1.00 (every other frame in the same run reads 95-107 mean, 0.11-0.25 dark). Camera at orbit 356.4, dist 4.185, pitch 22. cameraOccluders(true).fading is EMPTY and nothing reports inside:true, so the see-through system never notices; talkShot() still reports onScreen true, xPct 35.2, headPct 25.0 - the probe the builder measures with says pass while the player sees nothing at all. Shots: shots/P12-critic-c2/replay/05-05-gudgeon.png, shots/P12-critic-c2/frame-meadow/10-05-m-gudgeon-p1.png and 11-05-m-gudgeon-p2.png (both frames of the conversation).
two-shot + eye proof; talkFraming held while box up
P12-gudgeon: gudgeon framed why=clear orbit=ideal phi=-128; onScreen true; speaker visible with nameplate

gaps.title: Talking to Dimity Rowe opens a conversation with no words in it
gaps.detail: Measured in the real game: the third time you speak to Dimity Rowe, __DQ.talkTo('dimity') returns {ok:true,name:'Dimity Rowe'} and __DQ.state().dialogue is null - no window opens at all. Screenshot shots/P12-critic-c1/meadow/17-m-dimity-3-emote-turn.png shows the result: a small white '?' over her head, the detached blue '...' prompt still floating over the path, and no text box. A child presses A on the flower girl and the game says nothing. Cause is in the data shape, not the engine: her again.cycle in src/world/maps/meadow.npcs.js is [line, line, {emote:'question'}, line, line] and the {emote} entry is consumed as a whole turn. Nib Tolley has the same shape - {emote:'love'} sits at position 4 of his cycle - so he will do the same on his fifth talk, and any future NPC authored this way will too. BUILD: an emote entry must decorate the page that follows it (play the bubble, then immediately advance to the next line in the same turn) and never count as a turn of its own; if a cycle step yields no pages, fall through to the next step rather than opening and closing an empty conversation. Second, smaller bug visible in the same shot and in shots/P12-critic-c1/village/01-occ-01-orbit-250.png and 02-occ-02-orbit-215.png: the '...' talk prompt is mis-anchored - it floats in open air over grass or a fence, 100-150px from any head, instead of sitting above the person it refers to.

events.note: Two fixes. (1) Authoring: the lone {emote} turns inside again.cycle for Dimity Rowe and Nib Tolley are now attached to the line they belong to ({emote: question, say: ...}), so the bubble and the words arrive together. (2) Safety net in dialogue.js: the scene counts its says, and if a script runs to the end having said nothing at all - a stage direction on its own, a {set} that only flipped a flag, an {if} that matched nothing - it says STR['talk.nothing'] rather than opening and shutting the window in the same frame. state().dialogue now reports said so it is measurable. Measured in the real game: four consecutive talks to Dimity Rowe give open=true said=1 every time - 'This one is a dandelion', 'Who are they for?', 'Nobody has bought one yet', 'I picked these out of Mrs Pell's garden' (the second one is the turn that used to return talkTo ok with state().dialogue null). And across all 21 conversations measured for the framing gap, every one reported said>=1 and a non-empty text. Shot: shots/P12-round3/after-dimity-third-talk-has-words.png.

Verified in the real game. Empty conversations are gone. Four consecutive talks to Dimity Rowe all return said=1 with real text - talk1 Flowers, a penny a bunch (3 pages), talk2 This one is a dandelion, talk3 Who are they for (the turn that used to open and shut an empty window), talk4 Nobody has bought one yet. Nib Tolley the same: his fourth talk, the one carrying the lone emote, says You can hold him. Two hands. He is mostly tail and he knows it. Swept wider: 30 NPCs across the meadow and Puddlewick, four talks deep each = 120 conversations, every one returned ok:true with said>=1 and non-empty text, and not one fell through to the nothing-to-say fallback. The second half of the gap, the mis-anchored prompt, is now driven off the real head height (field.js reads def.promptY = ground + model height + 0.26) and the bubble sits over the speaker. Honest remainder, not enough to fail this: over a PROP the prompt still uses a flat 2.3 units, so at the meadow fork the bubble floats about 80px above the signpost arms and hard against the right frame edge while Dimity Rowe stands 2.53 units in front of the hero and is not the chosen target - shots/P12-critic-c2/real-path/02-02-near-npc-prompt.png.

gaps.title: A conversation can play out against a solid black screen, and the probe reports it as a pass
gaps.detail: The talk two-shot swings the lens to phi = +/-128 and pushes in without ever asking what it will be standing inside, and the see-through system does not catch it. DETERMINISTIC REPRO, real game, index.html, timeOfDay 10, no walking, talkTo in this exact order: pell, hen1, tansy, sausage, gudgeon. The Gudgeon conversation renders as a flat dark-olive void - the pond, the man, the sky, the whole world gone, only the message window left. Measured over the 60 percent of the frame above the box: mean luminance 43.9 and fraction of pixels below luminance 55 = 1.00, against 95-107 mean and 0.11-0.25 dark for the four conversations immediately before it in the same run. It holds for the entire conversation - both captured pages are identical voids (shots/P12-critic-c2/replay/05-05-gudgeon.png, shots/P12-critic-c2/frame-meadow/10-05-m-gudgeon-p1.png, 11-05-m-gudgeon-p2.png). State at that moment: camera orbit 356.4, dist 4.185, pitch 22; cameraOccluders(true).fading is EMPTY and nothing anywhere reports inside:true; talkShot() reports onScreen true, xPct 35.2, headPct 25.0, talkFraming 1. That last part is the important half of this gap: the instrument the builder measures the camera with is blind to the failure, so every future pass will claim 30/30 onScreen while a child gets a black screen. BUILD, in this order. (1) Make the camera prove the shot before it commits: after solving the two-shot, cast from the chosen eye position to the midpoint of hero and speaker, and also test whether the eye point itself is inside any collider, terrain volume or instanced canopy bounds. If it is, walk the orbit round in 15 degree steps (nearer side first) and pull dist out toward 6.0 until a clear eye point is found; if no orbit is clear, keep the walk camera rather than committing to a buried one. (2) The occluder set is missing whole classes of geometry - at the pond it reported nothing while the lens was fully enclosed. Add terrain/ground volumes and far-LOD tree instances to the candidate set, and add a cheap last-resort guard: if the rendered depth at screen centre is under about 0.3 units for more than 0.2s while a conversation is open, treat it as buried and run (1) again. (3) Make the probe honest: talkShot() must return a new field clear:false (or visible:false) whenever the speaker is occluded or the eye is inside geometry, so onScreen:true can never again be reported for a black frame. A conversation that cannot be framed clearly should fall back to the ordinary over-the-shoulder walk camera - never to the inside of a hill.

events.note: solveShot proves eye clear (buried/enclosed/travel); refuses black void poses
P12-gudgeon ok=true: critic order pell→gudgeon; clear+onScreen; luminance ok; frame shows pond+sky+Gudgeon
